title: Live stream melts the origin
description: A live sports stream publishes a new four-second segment every four seconds. Across 200 PoPs, about ten cache servers per PoP each fetch misses straight from the origin. At kickoff, the origin gets roughly 2,000 requests for every new segment and starts timing out. Which change most directly reduces that duplicate work?

options.text: Raise the segment TTL to one hour so it stays cached longer.
options.explanation: Each segment is new, so every request is a first miss; a longer TTL does nothing for objects that have never been cached.

options.text: Enable request collapsing on each server, hash keys to one owner server within each PoP, and route all PoP misses through an origin shield that also collapses.
options.explanation: Collapsing turns concurrent misses into one upstream fetch, in-PoP hashing makes each PoP miss once rather than once per server, and the shield makes the 200 PoPs miss once in total, so the origin sees roughly one request per segment.

options.text: Add the viewer's IP address to the cache key so each viewer gets a consistent copy.
options.explanation: That makes every viewer a cache miss and multiplies origin load.

options.text: Switch PoP routing from DNS to anycast.
options.explanation: Routing decides which PoP a viewer reaches; it does not change how many PoPs and servers miss to the origin.
